First listed 2025-10-13 · episode or wrap

Inside America’s Economic Divide: AI, Tariffs, & The Fed | The Real Eisman Playbook Episode 29

Eisman expresses a modest turn toward concern about a bifurcated economy, consumer stress and AI returns. His headline subtraction of total AI capex from annual GDP growth is invalid growth accounting and should not support the ex-AI stagnation thesis. Liesman offers qualified tariff concerns, acknowledges near-term resilience exceeded his expectations, discusses Fed political context, and ends with historical reflections on Russia. The episode repeatedly separates conditional mechanisms from precisely timed forecasts.

YouTube · 2025-10-13 ↗Substack · 2025-10-13 ↗
Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.

youtube-ZwoAJEzH99U-c002 · explanation

Subtracting over $400 billion of AI capex from roughly $530 billion implied GDP growth shows that the economy excluding AI is almost flat.

Wrong
Source · 1:46-2:41 ↗
SpeakerSteve Eisman
Stanceasserted
Horizonnot stated
Materialitymajor

The stated arithmetic is not a valid decomposition of GDP growth; this is a material error in the evidence offered for the core macro thesis.

Conditional reasoning

Even if all capex were domestic and prices constant, the investment contribution to annual growth would depend on I(t)-I(t-1), not I(t). If AI capex were $400b in both years, its direct growth contribution would be zero although the proposed subtraction removes $400b. Imports, overseas spending and inflation further prevent the claimed residual from measuring ex-AI real growth.

  • Annual GDP growth is a change in domestic output.
  • The cited AI capex is a total spending level, not its change from the prior year.
  • A real growth rate and current-dollar GDP are different price bases, and global capex includes foreign production.

Assessment test: Inspect the relevant original financial, operational or economic data and compare the claimed mechanism with competing explanations.

Further verification: Recheck the original data and subsequent realized outcomes.

Evidence and assessment details

Attribution confidence: high. Assessment confidence: medium. Thesis family: growth_accounting.

  • The expenditures approach to measuring GDP · 2025-06-03
    GDP measures domestic production; expenditure components contain imports that must be subtracted. Global company capex therefore is not automatically US GDP contribution.

Conditional reasoning

A valuable eventual technology can disappoint initially priced cash flows. Thus eventual adoption and wealth creation do not logically guarantee positive interim returns for all investors.

  • Investors pay prices reflecting expectations and financing costs.

Conditional reasoning

Observing not-B after replacement of A does not refute the implication A implies B. It can refute a separate forecast that A itself would persist, which must be evaluated separately.

  • A forecast states outcome B conditional on policy A.
  • Policy A is changed before the forecast can operate.

The conditional relationship follows from the explicit assumptions; it does not establish that those assumptions hold in observed markets.

Conditional reasoning

Landed input cost rises by the tariff amount. With output price and other costs fixed, the domestic producer's margin falls by that amount per unit of input used.

  • A producer uses an imported input at an unchanged pretariff price.
  • A positive tariff is paid and not offset by substitution, supplier concessions, exemption or another cost reduction.

How he reasons here

  • Separate markets, corporate margins and domestic output.
  • Use changes in domestic real investment when decomposing real GDP growth.
  • Test consumer stress across multiple credit and spending categories.
  • Evaluate policy forecasts under the policy actually specified.
  • Trace who captures technological returns and who finances the buildout.
  • Distinguish asset-price, employment and income-distribution channels.

Tools and charts discussed

Mentioned in the transcript; visual charts have not all been inspected.

  • GDP versus total AI capex arithmetic
  • CarMax and auto-credit warning indicators
  • Cruise versus hotel relative pricing
  • Statutory versus collected tariff rates
  • Fed communications and political constraints
  • Financial-crisis leverage/asset/interconnection mechanism
